title: Bourses du Gouvernement Français (BGF) - France Excellence Scholarships, Licence track
program_type: National government scholarship administered by ministry
administering_authority: Ministere de l'Europe et des Affaires etrangeres (French Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs)
implementing_agency: Campus France (Agence francaise pour la promotion de l'enseignement superieur, l'accueil et la mobilite internationale), implementing through the SCAC and Espaces Campus France of French embassies abroad
programme_action: Bourses du Gouvernement Francais / Bourses France Excellence - Licence (L1) track, awarded per country by French embassies and Espaces Campus France
description: The Bourses du Gouvernement Francais (BGF) are the scholarships of the French Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs, now published in embassy calls under the France Excellence label, that allow foreign nationals to study in French higher education institutions. They cover Licence (L1), Master and Doctorat levels, with the Licence track funding the first year of higher education. Campus France pays a monthly maintenance allowance on an official government rate grid: EUR 900 for the Licence and Master rates and EUR 1,850 for the doctorate rate. Holders are exempted from the CVEC and from enrolment fees for national degrees in public establishments, and receive social security registration plus support for accommodation and travel.

programme_structure.allocation: Per-country quota set by the French embassy / Espace Campus France and its partner ministry; the French Foreign Ministry directly funds only a minority of its scholarships (France Excellence Eiffel and France Excellence Major) and the rest are provided by French embassies abroad
programme_structure.quota: Embassy-specific; some calls set an explicit number of awards, others do not publish a quota
programme_structure.host_institutions: Any French public higher education institution connected to the national admission procedure (Parcoursup for Licence 1); the Bulgarian call states awards are for degree-granting programmes in France taught in French or English
award_categories: Licence (L1) - 10 months of funding for the first year of higher education, open to final-year secondary-school students
Doctorat - cotutelle / international co-direction, three 4-month stays in the cotutelle model
Language scholarships (Bourses linguistiques) - separate call, not degree-level

status_note: The BGF scheme is continuous, with each French embassy opening its own application call. Most country calls for the 2026/2027 academic year closed between April and June 2026 (Croatia 30 April 2026, Bulgaria 23 April 2026, Togo 24 May 2026, Albania 29 May 2026, Cote d'Ivoire 31 May 2026 for Master and 4 June 2026 for Doctorat). Calls for the 2027/2028 academic year are expected from late 2026 onwards. The 2026/2027 Croatian call was published with an extended deadline, confirming the rolling nature of the programme.
verification_notes: Verified against the French Ministry's implementing agency Campus France (campusfrance.org), the Institut francais de Bulgarie (institutfrancais.bg) and the Croatian Espace Campus France (croatie.campusfrance.org), plus the MEAE-hosted Cambodia notice PDF and the Florence Institut francais page. The monthly rate grid (EUR 900 Licence/Master, EUR 1,850 Doctorat) and the CVEC/enrolment-fee exoneration were taken directly from the Campus France scholarship-holder guide updated 10 April 2026. The Licence-level eligibility, documents and deadline were taken from the Bulgarian France Excellence 2027 call. Because deadlines and eligibility are set per country, no single central deadline exists for the award as a whole.

application_deadline.typical_application_window: January to June depending on the country call; many European calls fall in April, while calls for the 2026/2027 academic year closed between 30 April 2026 and 4 June 2026
application_deadline.application_period: Country calls open roughly January-March and close mostly between April and June; Italian and French institutional routes differ
application_deadline.official_rule: There is no single central deadline. Each French embassy and Espace Campus France publishes its own call with its own date. Verified examples for 2026/2027: Croatia 30 April 2026 (extended), Bulgaria 23 April 2026, Togo 24 May 2026, Albania 29 May 2026, Cote d'Ivoire 31 May 2026 (Master) and 4 June 2026 (Doctorat). Applicants must consult the Campus France office for their country.
application_deadline.deadline_warning: Deadlines vary by country and are published in the local language on the local Espace Campus France or embassy site; missing the national call usually means waiting a full year. No timezone is published for these deadlines.

programme_duration.official_range: 10 months for the Licence track (one academic year of the Licence)
programme_duration.renewal_note: The Licence award funds the first year of higher education only. The Bulgaria 2027 call states that after one full year of study in France students can apply for a CROUS grant to continue their studies. Any extension of the initial scholarship period is decided by the ministry or embassy and must be requested at least three months before expiry.

funding.scholarship_type: Monthly maintenance allowance plus statutory fee exoneration (not a tuition grant)
funding.monthly_amount_note: Official Campus France rate grid (guide updated 10 April 2026): 'Taux licence et master 900 EUR' / 'Bachelor's and Master's degree rate EUR 900'. The doctorate rate is EUR 1,850. The Bulgarian France Excellence 2027 call independently lists 900 EUR for licences.
funding.travel_amount_note: No euro amount is published. Campus France states that if the international trip is financed by the Ministry or an embassy, Campus France books the plane ticket in economy class and sends the e-ticket by email. The Bulgarian call also covers domestic transportation in France to reach the assigned city. In the Croatian call the round-trip airfare is instead paid by the Croatian Agency for Mobility and EU Programmes.
funding.fully_funded_note: Not a full-cost award. It provides a maintenance allowance, statutory exoneration of the CVEC and enrolment fees for national degrees in public establishments, social security registration and support for travel and accommodation. Formation and tuition fees are explicitly not reimbursed by Campus France and remain the student's responsibility.

tuition.conditions: Exoneration of enrolment fees for the preparation of a national degree or a graduated engineering degree in public scientific, cultural and professional establishments under the Minister for Higher Education (Article R719-49 of the Education Code), on presentation of the Campus France scholarship attestation. Not a cash payment and not applicable to private institutions.

monthly_stipend.conditions: Monthly maintenance allowance at the 'licence' rate, paid at the beginning of each month from the date of arrival in France, calculated on the dates of presence in France and limited to the duration of the scholarship. Amount is set by the official government rate grid and cannot be modified.

travel_allowance.conditions: International airfare in economy class booked by Campus France when the trip is funded by the Ministry or the embassy; ticket is date-fixed and generally not modifiable. Bulgarian call also covers transport within France to the assigned city.

installation_allowance.note: No separate installation or settling-in allowance is published. Accommodation search support and (in Bulgaria) domestic transport are provided instead.

visa_support.conditions: Recipients hold the status of boursier du gouvernement francais; the Cambodian notice states that for social-coverage scholarship holders this status carries visa fee exoneration, personalised welcome in France, priority housing in university residences and administrative assistance.

insurance.conditions: Mandatory and free registration with the French general social security scheme via etudiant-etranger.ameli.fr. Until affiliation, free provisional cover is provided by an insurer appointed by Campus France, limited to two months after arrival. The insurance covers the scholarship holder only, not family members.

research_allowance.note: Not applicable to the Licence track.

family_allowance.note: Not published in official source. Campus France states accommodation is reserved for the beneficiary only and does not apply to accompanied applicants.

accommodation_support.conditions: On request in the personal Campus France space, Campus France proposes accommodation adapted to the situation, in most cases a CROUS university residence. Booking fees and monthly rent are charged, with the residence bills paid by Campus France and the student's contribution deducted directly from the monthly allowance. Ancillary costs (meals, laundry, bar) remain the student's responsibility.

bond.note: No service bond or return-of-service obligation is published for the BGF. Obligations are academic: assiduous participation, compliance with the host institution's rules and sitting examinations, plus transmission of the enrolment certificate, semester evaluation and exam results.

total_estimated_value.note: No total award value is published by the official source. The official figures are the monthly rate of EUR 900 and the doctorate rate of EUR 1,850; no aggregate is published and none is computed here.

cultural_activities.conditions: Campus France offers many activities at preferential rates, with part of the cost covered by the Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs: discovery of French heritage and regions, short stays in Europe, shows, workshops and sports courses.

coverage: Monthly maintenance allowance of EUR 900 for the Licence (L1) rate
Exoneration of the CVEC (Contribution Vie etudiante et de Campus)
Exoneration of enrolment fees for national degrees and graduated engineering degrees in public establishments (Article R719-49 of the Education Code)
Mandatory and free registration with the French general social security scheme
Provisional free health cover by a Campus France-appointed insurer for up to two months after arrival
International airfare in economy class booked by Campus France when funded by the Ministry or embassy
Accommodation search support, generally a CROUS university residence
Cultural activities and short European stays at preferential rates
coverage_limitations: Campus France explicitly does not reimburse enrolment or tuition/formation fees paid directly to the institution; these remain the student's responsibility
The monthly allowance is fixed by an official government rate grid and cannot be modified

The exact benefit structure differs per country and per embassy call - for example in the Croatian call the return airfare is paid by the Croatian Agency for Mobility and EU Programmes, not by the French side
Accommodation support is subject to CROUS availability and the student's contribution is deducted from the allowance
Provisional health cover cannot exceed two months after arrival and does not cover family members
The Licence award funds the first year only; continuation requires a separate CROUS application
Private institutions and non-national degrees are not covered by the statutory fee exoneration
eligible_applicants: Foreign nationals who are not French citizens, applying through the call published by the French embassy or Espace Campus France in their country
For the Licence track: candidates in their final year of secondary education, regularly enrolled in a secondary establishment on the territory of the applicant country
Applicants who have submitted or will submit the corresponding national admission application (Parcoursup for Licence 1 in the Bulgarian call)
Applicants not already receiving another French government scholarship or institutional funding for the same period
final_year_condition: Not applicable in the bachelor's sense: the Licence track is for secondary-school leavers entering the first year of higher education, not for final-year bachelor's students. The Bulgarian 2027 call requires applicants to be regularly enrolled in a secondary establishment in Bulgaria and to hold certificates covering grades 8 to 11 plus the first semester of grade 12. Applicants for the Master track must instead have validated three or four years of higher education or be enrolled in the final year of a Licence or Master 1.
equivalent_degree_note: For the Licence track, applicants must have a secondary-school leaving qualification; the Bulgarian call requires the 'Certificat de fin d'etudes secondaires - premiere etape'. Foreign qualifications are generally accepted subject to the equivalence rules of the specific national call, which must be confirmed with the local Espace Campus France.

age_limit.official_source: Bulgaria France Excellence 2027 call: 'etre majeur pour la licence (L1)' (must be of legal age, i.e. 18+); Croatia BGF 2026/2027 call: 'stipendije su namijenjene drzavljanima Republike Hrvatske koji su rodeni nakon 31. prosinca 1990. godine' (Croatian citizens born after 31 December 1990)

nationality_quota: Awards are allocated per country by the French embassy and Espace Campus France, often as part of bilateral cooperation (for example the Croatian call is run with the Croatian Ministry of Science, Education and Youth and the Agency for Mobility and EU Programmes). Quotas are set nationally and are not published centrally.
previous_award_restriction: Previous holders of the same BGF scholarship type cannot re-apply for the same award: the Croatian 2026/2027 call states 'Kandidati koji su prethodno bili dobitnici ove stipendije nemaju pravo ponovne prijave za istu vrstu stipendije'. Candidates already receiving another scholarship or institutional financial support for the study period covered by the call are not eligible. Eiffel applicants already holding a French government scholarship are likewise ineligible for Eiffel.

eligibility.citizenship: National-only per call: the applicant must hold the nationality of the country whose embassy publishes the call (verified for Croatia and Bulgaria). Dual French nationals are excluded in some calls.
eligibility.residence_requirement: Usually residence in the applicant country: the Bulgaria 2027 call requires applicants to 'etre de nationalite bulgare et resider en Bulgarie'.
eligibility.age_limit: Licence track: must be of legal age (18 or over) per the Bulgaria call. The Croatian 2026/2027 call requires candidates born after 31 December 1990.
eligibility.secondary_school_requirement: Licence track: regular enrolment in a secondary establishment in the applicant country, with transcripts for grades 8, 9, 10, 11 and the first semester of grade 12 plus the secondary-school completion certificate.
eligibility.academic_requirements: Excellent academic results. The Bulgaria call explicitly requires 'Excellents resultats scolaires' for the Licence track.
eligibility.gpa_requirement: No universal GPA or percentage threshold is published by the official sources; evaluation is on academic excellence and the quality of the study plan.
eligibility.language_requirement: Licence track in Bulgaria: a DELF B2 or DALF C1 diploma is required, and 'une tres bonne maitrise de la langue francaise' is necessary. Croatian call: excellent knowledge of the language of instruction is a qualitative criterion; French is an advantage but not a condition. Cambodian co-funded doctorate: B2 equivalent English for programmes taught in English.
eligibility.work_experience: Not required for the Licence track.
eligibility.extracurricular_requirement: Not published as a formal requirement.
eligibility.leadership_requirement: Not published as a formal requirement.
eligibility.financial_need: Not a criterion. The BGF is an excellence-based scholarship; financial need is not listed among the award criteria in the Bulgarian or Croatian calls.
eligibility.previous_scholarship_restriction: Previous holders of the same scholarship type cannot re-apply; applicants already receiving another scholarship or institutional funding for the period are not eligible.
eligibility.enrolment_status_requirement: Licence applicants must currently be secondary-school students. Master applicants must have validated three or four years of higher education or be enrolled in the final year of a Licence or Master 1. Doctorate applicants must be enrolled in a doctoral programme.
eligibility.health_requirement: No specific health requirement published. All non-EU/EEA/Swiss students must register with French social security.
eligibility.field_restrictions: The Bulgarian Licence track excludes medicine ('ces bourses ne peuvent pas etre attribuees aux candidats pour des etudes en medecine'). Other calls are open to all fields, sometimes with priority fields named for that year (for example Croatia 2026/2027 gives priority to technical and high-technology sciences, STEM, digital technology, ICT, biotechnology and biomedicine).

academic_requirements.percentage_note: No fixed percentage, class rank or GPA threshold is published in the official sources for the BGF Licence track.
academic_requirements.programme_specific_requirements: Bulgaria Licence track: transcripts for grades 8, 9, 10, 11 and the first semester of grade 12, plus the secondary-school completion certificate; a DELF B2 or DALF C1 diploma; a Parcoursup application must have been filed. Master track: three or four validated years of higher education or current enrolment in Licence 3 or Master 1.
selection_factors_may_include: Quality of the study plan and clearly defined objectives of the stay
Impact of the mobility and importance of the stay in France for professional development
Impact of the mobility on strengthening cooperation between the home and host institutions
Knowledge of the language of instruction
academic_requirements.holistic_selection_note: Selection is on academic excellence combined with the quality and relevance of the study project. The Bulgarian jury 'est souverain et determine lui-meme ses criteres de selection'.

english_requirement.test_score_note: No universal English test threshold is published for the BGF. The Cambodian co-funded notice states that for programmes taught in English candidates must provide proof of English proficiency at a level equivalent to B2, or hold a French bachelor's or master's degree whose courses were taught in English. Requirements are set per national call.
accepted_tests: DELF B2 (diploma required for the Bulgarian Licence track)
DALF C1 (accepted for the Bulgarian Licence track)
Proof of English proficiency equivalent to B2 for English-taught programmes (Cambodian co-funded notice)

language_of_instruction.language_note: The Bulgaria 2027 call states the scholarships are awarded for degree-granting programmes in France 'en francais ou en anglais' (in French or English). The Licence track in Bulgaria additionally requires a DELF B2 or DALF C1 diploma and very good command of French.

application_method.application_route: Apply directly to the French embassy or Espace Campus France in your country in response to its published call, either by email or by depositing the paper file at the institute; the Campus France local office manages the BGF calls published by the embassies.
application_steps: Find the BGF / France Excellence call published by the French embassy or Espace Campus France for your country
Check eligibility (nationality, age, education level, fields)
In parallel, file the corresponding admission application (Parcoursup for Licence 1 in the Bulgarian call; Etudes en France platform where required)
Complete the BGF application form and assemble the documents, translated and certified
Submit the file to the embassy or institute before the national deadline
After selection, submit the Dossier de bourse d'etudes to the local office, which forwards it to Campus France
On arrival in France, notify Campus France to trigger the first allowance
application_method.application_fee_note: No application fee is published for the BGF scholarship call itself. Note that separate admission platforms charge their own fees: the Madagascar Horizon notice references paying a half-price fee for the Etudes en France platform, and the Lebanese page references an Institut francais validation fee of about EUR 320 for files validated outside the Campus France procedure. These are admission fees, not BGF scholarship fees.

universal_documents: Completed and signed BGF application form with a photograph attached
Copy of the identity card or passport
Curriculum vitae (CV) in French or English
Motivation letter presenting the project and objective of the candidate
commonly_requested_documents: Transcripts of the last completed and current level of study
Diploma of the highest completed level of education
Proof of language proficiency (DELF B2 / DALF C1 for the Bulgarian Licence track)
Acceptance letter or proof of contact with the French host institution
secondary_school_documents: Transcripts for grades 8, 9, 10, 11 and the first semester of grade 12 (Bulgarian Licence call)
Certificat de fin d'etudes secondaires - premiere etape (Bulgarian Licence call)
official_application_documents.document_language: Applications must be submitted in English or French. In the Bulgarian call all documents except the identity card must be translated into French; diplomas, transcripts and official certificates must be translated by a translation agency with signature and stamp (no legalisation required), while the CV, motivation letter and recommendations may be translated by the candidate into French or English.
official_application_documents.document_format: Electronic submission by email, or paper file deposited at the institute. The Croatian call specifies PDF, Doc and JPG formats for emailed files, and candidates may be asked to produce the original documents.
official_application_documents.transcript_requirement: Transcripts of the last completed and current level of study are required for all tracks.
official_application_documents.certified_translation_note: Diplomas, transcripts and official certificates must be translated by a translation agency with the translator's signature and stamp (legalisation not required) per the Bulgarian call. Non-certified copies of the passport/ID card do not require translation.

identity_documents.note: Bulgarian call: an uncertified copy is accepted and does not need translation into French or English.

identity_documents.item: Photograph attached to the application form
identity_documents.note: Explicitly listed in the Bulgarian call.

academic_documents.item: Secondary-school transcripts for grades 8, 9, 10, 11 and the first semester of grade 12
Certificat de fin d'etudes secondaires - premiere etape
Enrolment certificate for the current level of study
academic_documents.note: Required for applicants currently enrolled at any level.

academic_documents.item: Diploma of the highest completed level of education
academic_documents.note: Required for the Master track; for the Licence track the secondary-school certificate applies instead.

language_documents.item: DELF B2 or DALF C1 diploma
language_documents.note: Explicitly required for the Bulgarian Licence track.

language_documents.item: Proof of knowledge of French or English depending on the language of instruction
language_documents.note: Croatian call: desirable but not a compulsory part of the application file.

language_documents.item: Proof of English proficiency equivalent to B2 for English-taught programmes
language_documents.note: Cambodian co-funded notice; alternatively a French bachelor's or master's taught in English.

application_essays.item: Motivation letter presenting the project and objective of the candidate
application_essays.note: Bulgarian Licence track: the letter must obligatorily list the other wishes formulated on the Parcoursup platform.

financial_documents.item: No financial documents are required for the Licence track
financial_documents.note: The BGF is excellence-based and does not require proof of financial need. Co-financed variants may ask for a co-funding letter.

additional_documents.item: Proof of the Parcoursup application (Licence 1 route)
additional_documents.note: Bulgarian Licence track: candidates must have filed their applications on Parcoursup.

additional_documents.item: Acceptance letter from the French institution, or proof of contact with it
additional_documents.note: Croatian call: acceptance letter or correspondence evidencing established contact with the chosen institution.
Croatian call: completed online then printed and signed, submitted to both the French Embassy and the Agency for Mobility and EU Programmes.

required_documents: Completed and signed BGF application form with photograph
Copy of identity card or passport
Curriculum vitae (CV) in English or French
Transcripts of the last completed and current level of study
Diploma of the highest completed qualification (or enrolment certificate if in progress)
Secondary-school transcripts and secondary-school completion certificate (Licence track)
DELF B2 or DALF C1 diploma (Bulgarian Licence track)
Motivation letter stating the project and objective, listing Parcoursup wishes (Licence track)
Proof of the Parcoursup or Etudes en France application (Licence track)
Acceptance letter or proof of contact with the French host institution
Certified translations of diplomas, transcripts and official certificates

selection_process.decision_maker: A mixed national commission. Bulgaria: a jury of Bulgarian academics and representatives of the Institut francais de Bulgarie, which is sovereign and sets its own criteria. Croatia: a commission composed of representatives of the French Embassy, the Croatian Ministry of Science, Education and Youth and the Agency for Mobility and EU Programmes, whose decision is final.
selection_process.selection_type: Dossier review followed by interview for pre-selected candidates; some calls (Cambodia) evaluate both file quality and oral performance.
possible_stages: Submission of the application file to the embassy or Espace Campus France
Completeness and eligibility check (incomplete files are not examined)
Dossier review by the national mixed commission
Interview of pre-selected candidates (Bulgaria: 11 May for Licence, 12 May for Master and Doctorat)
Submission of the Dossier de bourse d'etudes following final acceptance by the French institution
selection_process.weighting_note: No universal weighting is published. Each national jury determines its own criteria; the Bulgarian jury is explicitly sovereign in setting its selection criteria.
selection_process.results_timing: Bulgaria 2027 call: interviews 11 and 12 May 2026, selected candidates then file the Dossier de bourse d'etudes in June/July 2026. Croatia 2026/2027 call: all candidates informed of the outcome by email no later than the end of May 2026. Cambodian notice: panel meets in May 2026, results published June 2026.
selection_process.scholarship_rank_note: The Bulgarian licence allocation is a fixed EUR 900 rate; no ranking is published. The Croatian commission's decision is final and not subject to further modification.

additional_factors: Quality of the study plan and clearly defined objectives of the stay
Impact of the mobility and the importance of the stay in France for the candidate's professional development
Impact of the mobility on strengthening cooperation between the candidate's home institution and the host institution in France
Knowledge of the language in which the study or training is conducted
Priority fields set by the call (Croatia 2026/2027: technical and high-technology sciences, STEM, digital technology, ICT, biotechnology and biomedicine)
Presence of co-financing favoured in some calls (Cambodia)
selection_criteria.source: institutfrancais.bg Bulgaria France Excellence 2027 call and croatie.campusfrance.org Croatia BGF 2026/2027 call

degree_outcome.awarded_qualification: Licence (French national bachelor's degree) at the host French institution
degree_outcome.typical_programme_length: A Licence is a three-year degree (six semesters); the BGF Licence award funds the first year only (10 months in the Bulgarian call)
possible_awards: Doctorat via cotutelle (three 4-month stays) or international co-direction (short stays)
degree_outcome.degree_note: The scholarship is granted for a specific duration, a precisely identified programme, a specific diploma and a specific institution. Any change of institution or reorientation must be submitted to Campus France and analysed by the ministry or embassy that awarded the scholarship, which decides whether to maintain the benefit.
degree_outcome.credit_transfer: Not published for the BGF itself. Admission to Licence 1 is handled through the national Parcoursup procedure in the Bulgarian call, with university responses due before 30 April.

student_rights_and_cost_protection.tuition_fee_for_recipients: Exoneration of the CVEC and of enrolment fees for national degrees and graduated engineering degrees in public establishments, on presentation of the Campus France scholarship attestation. Formation and tuition fees are not covered and remain the student's responsibility; Campus France does not reimburse fees paid directly to the institution.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.application_fee_for_recipients: No application fee is charged for the BGF call itself. Admission platforms charge their own fees separately.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.student_agreement_note: Recipients sign a 'dossier de bourse d'etudes' before departure that sets out their obligations. Bulgaria: the scholarship may be called into question during the stay, as French government scholarship holders are subject to attendance and academic excellence requirements.
common_services: Dedicated Campus France contact given in the Pass Campus France
Free registration with the French general social security scheme
Provisional free health cover for up to two months after arrival
Economy-class international airfare booked by Campus France
Cultural activities, heritage discovery and short European stays at preferential rates
France Alumni network membership after the scholarship
student_rights_and_cost_protection.bond_breach_consequence: No service bond applies. Non-compliance with the obligations (assiduous participation in the programme, compliance with the host institution's rules, sitting examinations, transmitting the enrolment certificate, semester evaluation and exam results, keeping the address up to date) may result in suspension of the scholarship-holder status and of the related benefits (CVEC and fee exoneration, health cover, CROUS housing). Payment of the allowance may also be suspended for unjustified absence or behaviour incompatible with the status. In case of failure, the ministry or embassy may terminate the scholarship.

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm that your country publishes a BGF / France Excellence call covering the Licence level (not all countries do)
Confirm your nationality and residence match the call's requirements
Confirm you are in your final year of secondary education and are of legal age
Secure a DELF B2 or DALF C1 (or the language qualification specified by the call)
File the national admission application (Parcoursup for Licence 1) in parallel
Collect transcripts for grades 8-12 and the secondary-school completion certificate
Write the motivation letter including the list of Parcoursup wishes
Submit the file before the national deadline and keep proof of submission
programme_comparison_fields: Whether the country call covers the Licence level at all
Duration of the award (10 months for Licence)
Whether travel and accommodation are covered and by which side
Required French level (DELF B2 / DALF C1 in the Bulgarian call)
Whether the applicant must already hold or file the national admission application
practical_application_data.motivation_letter_strategy: The motivation letter must present the project and the objective pursued, and in the Bulgarian Licence track it must obligatorily list the other wishes formulated on Parcoursup. It should explain the choice of study and institution, the expected outcome for the candidate's professional development, and the impact of the mobility on cooperation between the home and host institutions.
profile_fit_labels: Final-year secondary-school student with strong grades
National of a country whose embassy runs a BGF Licence call
common_mistakes: Assuming a single central deadline - calls are per country and vary between April and June
Assuming the BGF covers all countries or all study levels - many calls are Master and Doctorat only
Applying for medicine in Bulgaria, where the Licence award excludes medical studies
Failing to file the national admission application (Parcoursup) in parallel with the scholarship call
Submitting documents without certified French translations
Omitting the list of Parcoursup wishes from the motivation letter
Assuming tuition is paid - formation fees remain the student's responsibility
Applying while already holding another French government scholarship for the same period

risk_flags.risk: No Licence call exists in the applicant's country
risk_flags.impact: The applicant cannot use the BGF for a bachelor's degree and must find an alternative
risk_flags.mitigation: Check the local Espace Campus France / embassy site early; the Campus France country directory lists every Espace. Several calls are Master and Doctorat only.

risk_flags.risk: Per-country deadlines vary widely and are published only in local languages
risk_flags.impact: A missed or misunderstood deadline means waiting a full academic year
risk_flags.mitigation: Verify the exact date and language on the local Espace Campus France site well in advance; the Croatian call was republished with an extended deadline, so late calls can appear.

risk_flags.impact: Travel or accommodation support assumed from one country's call may not apply in another
risk_flags.mitigation: Read the specific notice and explanatory note for the country call; confirm with the Espace Campus France by email before relying on a benefit.

risk_flags.impact: Applicants without DELF B2 or DALF C1 are ineligible for the Bulgarian Licence track
risk_flags.mitigation: Obtain the certification in the penultimate year of secondary school, or target a country call that accepts English-taught programmes.

risk_flags.impact: Medical studies are excluded from the Bulgarian Licence award
risk_flags.mitigation: Confirm field restrictions in the country call before applying.

risk_flags.impact: Private institutions and non-national degrees carry full cost
risk_flags.mitigation: Budget beyond the EUR 900 monthly allowance; the statutory fee exoneration applies only to national degrees in public establishments.

risk_flags.risk: Scholarship can be suspended or terminated
risk_flags.impact: Loss of allowance and benefits during the stay
risk_flags.mitigation: Send the enrolment certificate on arrival, the social security certificate within three months, and exam results each year; notify Campus France immediately of any change of situation.

risk_flags.risk: Previous BGF holders are barred from re-applying for the same type
risk_flags.impact: A prior award in the same category blocks a repeat application
risk_flags.mitigation: Apply for the correct track and time the application to avoid overlap with a previous award.

application_status_workflow: Call published by the embassy or Espace Campus France
Application submitted to the embassy or institute
Dossier review by the national commission
Dossier de bourse d'etudes submitted via the local office to Campus France
Arrival in France and first allowance payment triggered
Annual monitoring, results transmission and possible extension request
best_fit: Final-year secondary-school students of a country whose French embassy or Espace Campus France runs a France Excellence / BGF call covering the Licence level, with excellent grades, a certified French level of B2 or C1, and a project to start a Licence in France through Parcoursup.
not_best_fit: Applicants whose country's call covers only Master and Doctorat levels
Applicants already holding another French government scholarship for the same period
Applicants seeking full tuition coverage (formation fees are not reimbursed)
Applicants without a secondary-school leaving qualification
Applicants under the legal age of majority
Medical applicants in Bulgaria, where medical studies are excluded
Applicants looking for a scholarship with no interview or no French requirement

image.logo_verification_method: The Campus France logo is served from the agency's own domain as the header mark on every campusfrance.org page, including the officially published BGF scholarship-holder guide page. A HEAD request to the asset URL returned HTTP 200 with Content-Type image/png and Content-Length 6826. The complementary Republique francaise mark (logo-republique-francaise.svg) is also hosted on the same official domain and returned HTTP 200 with Content-Type image/svg+xml. No third-party, aggregator, Wikipedia, news or stock source was used. The awarding authority is the French Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs; Campus France is the official implementing agency that manages these scholarships, so the Campus France mark is the correct logo for the award's administering body.
image.image_usage_note: No photograph is recorded. The official pages use a Shutterstock-licensed photograph that cannot be hotlinked or reused.

database_notes: Substitution: none. The assigned target (France, Bourses du Gouvernement Francais) is not on the do-not-duplicate list, is hosted in an allowed region (Europe) and is a bachelor's-level award, so it was researched as assigned.

Branding note: the same scheme is published under two names. Embassy calls now use the France Excellence / BFE label ('France Excellence Scholarships (BFE) - formerly BGF', per the French Embassy in Cambodia notice), while Campus France and the Bulgarian and Croatian pages still use 'Bourses du Gouvernement Francais'. Both are recorded in legacy_titles.

Degree-level scope: the BGF covers Licence (L1), Master and Doctorat. This record documents the Licence (bachelor's) track, as required by the bachelor's contract. Master and Doctorat coverage is noted in funding_breakdown and programme_structure rather than in the degree fields.

The awarding body is per country: the French Foreign Ministry directly funds only part of its scholarships (France Excellence Eiffel and France Excellence Major), and the rest are provided by French embassies abroad (campusfrance.org). This is why the record has no single deadline.

Applicant regions researched: Croatia (Espace Campus France Croatie), Bulgaria (Institut francais de Bulgarie) and, for the co-funded bilateral naming and the English-taught route, Cambodia (Embassy of France in Cambodia on diplomatie.gouv.fr).

bourse.gouv.fr, cited in the assignment, returned a transport error on 2026-10-10 and could not be read. All benefit and eligibility data in this record come instead from campusfrance.org, institutfrancais.bg, croatie.campusfrance.org and diplomatie.gouv.fr.

The ministry page diplomatie.gouv.fr/en/coming-to-france/studying-in-france/finance-your-studies-scholarships/ could not be connected to from this environment; the equivalent campusfrance.org pages were used instead and the embassy-hosted Cambodian PDF from the diplomatie.gouv.fr domain was retrieved successfully.

Amounts: EUR 900 per month for the Licence rate is taken verbatim from the Campus France official rate grid and corroborated by the Bulgarian France Excellence 2027 call (900 EUR for licences). The doctorate rate of EUR 1,850 is recorded for completeness only.

Logo: the Campus France logo on campusfrance.org's own domain was verified by HTTP 200 response with Content-Type image/png. This is the implementing agency's mark for the award, which the schema permits; a photo was not recorded because the official pages use a Shutterstock-licensed image.

Deadlines earlier than 2026-10-10 mean most 2026/2027 country calls are now closed; the record is therefore set to status ONGOING rather than OPEN, and the next cycle is expected from late 2026 onwards.

The Croatian 2026/2027 call text states the deadline as 30 April 2026 while also mentioning receipt 'no later than 31 March 2026 at 23:59' in its timeliness clause; the headline date of 30 April 2026 is used and the inconsistency is flagged for re-verification.
No age cap is published for the Licence track; the only age rule found is the minimum legal age of 18 in the Bulgarian call, so age_limit.maximum_age is null rather than invented.
No GPA, class-rank or English-test threshold is published universally for the BGF; all such fields are null or marked programme-specific rather than filled with a plausible value.
